correctness.rationale: The Walsh characters give d+1 distinct energy levels since J>0. The space spanned level by level by projections of the two sink vectors reduces both H and the loss operator; its orthogonal complement evolves unitarily. An eigenvector in the bright space with real effective energy would have zero amplitude at both sinks by taking imaginary parts and using strict positivity of the losses. It would then belong to a single H eigenspace and be orthogonal to both sink projections in that eigenspace, a contradiction. Dissipativity excludes positive imaginary energy and in finite dimension all bright Jordan blocks decay. For a nonantipodal pair and an interior Walsh weight k, choose one index in the support of s and one outside; keep a fixed k−1 subset of the remaining d−2 indices and exchange the two chosen indices. This produces opposite parities of overlap with s, so the signed count has strict modulus less than C_k and the interior Gram ranks are two. The extreme ranks are one. For antipodes the vectors are collinear in every level with sign (−1)^k. The Gram inverse with entries 2^(-d)(C_k,K_k(h)) and sink overlaps 2^(-d)(K_k(w),K_k(z)) gives the displayed localized probabilities, including 2/2^d from the extreme levels in the nonantipodal case. The normalized projection trace gives both dimension-five and general averages. Numerical evolution in the bundled script was inspected but not executed; the decay claim rests on the reducing subspaces and spectral argument.
residual_risks: This proves eventual loss only for the positive-rate finite model, not its speed or its stability as a rate tends to zero.
